name: Mistakes that point to the fix

sources.name: Objection-first listicle (lead with the category's top objection)

sections.hero: Dek: name what the reader misses out on by repeating these mistakes.
sections.items: Each item: the mistake, what it costs the reader, then what the product does instead -- three short beats.
sections.audience_fit: Not-for-you names real limits, so the fix never reads as a hard sell.
sections.closing: Recap the three biggest mistakes; the product appears as the fix, not a slogan.

items.heading_hint: The category's biggest objection, framed as a mistake
Relying on access you do not control (schedules, travel)
Picking an option that lacks something the reader needs
Assuming setup is harder than the verified facts say
Comparing on price alone and skipping warranty and delivery terms

voice: Candid coach, second person, short sentences; no blame, no fear.
compliance: Every number, price, spec or outcome needs a verified claim_id; a hint is never a fact.
No health or outcome promise for the product; a health statement cites the study and its population.
Never name or criticise a competitor brand; a mistake is about a category or a habit.
writer_brief: Each item is a mistake, its cost and the fix. The product enters as the fix inside an item, never as a slogan. Verified claims only.
